rationale: wu_2015_trainable-claude-agentic: wu_n_bands=6, wu_n_outer=2, wu_motion_range=8, wu_motion_window=3, epochs=12, batch_size=1, lr=0.00011, weight_decay=0.0, loss_base=mse, lambda_neg=0.7, wu_soft_thresh=0.0015, wu_sigmoid_slope=10.0, wu_sigmoid_offset=1.0, wu_band_scale=1.0, wu_residual_blend=1.0, train_n=600, val_n=200, val_chunk=4, seed=42, rationale=ITER-4 (one knob vs iter-1 best). NUMBERS: iter-1 hr=0.3009 (n_bands=6,n_outer=2,motion_window=2 BEST); iter-2 hr=0.2805 (n_bands=8 worse); iter-3 hr=0.0 (n_outer=3 COLLAPSE -- classical instability recurs even at low TPE lr, so n_outer=2 is LOCKED). FAILURE MODE: both architecture-capacity knobs (more bands, more outer stages) hurt -> the band/residual structure is at its expressivity optimum at (6,2). Remaining productive lever = the motion-compensated feature-preserving interpolation that denoises the residual sinogram; wu_motion_window controls the L1 patch half-width. Prior TPE moved it 1->2; window=3 UNTESTED. ONE KNOB: wu_motion_window 2 -> 3 (structural int, NO new params -> stays 12 trainable scalars). Base = iter-1. HYPOTHESIS: if I widen the motion-window to 3, I expect val hr to rise above 0.3009 because a larger L1 matching patch gives a more robust residual-motion estimate (less noise leakage into the residual reco before soft-thresholding), improving the refinement stage; risk = over-smoothing the residual detail (hr flat or slightly down). Budget: window is a small per-pixel patch cost on iter-1s 819s base -> fits 20 min.
